subject: Mathematics
title: Graphs of Linear Equations and Simultaneous Linear Equations
learningOutcomes: Find the gradient of a straight line and state its y-intercept from \(y = mx + c\).
Draw the graph of a linear equation in the form \(ax + by = k\).
Interpret distance–time graphs, where the gradient is the speed.
Solve simultaneous linear equations using the graphical method.
Solve simultaneous linear equations using the elimination and substitution methods.
Form and solve a pair of linear equations from a real-world word problem.

sections.heading: Gradient and y-intercept
sections.body: A straight line is written as \(y = mx + c\). Here \(m\) is the gradient (steepness) and \(c\) is the y-intercept (where the line cuts the y-axis). The gradient is found from \(m = \frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\). A line sloping up from left to right has a positive gradient; sloping down gives a negative gradient.

sections.heading: Drawing ax + by = k
sections.body: To draw a linear equation, make a table of values: choose a few \(x\) values, work out each \(y\), plot the points and join them with a ruler. Only two points are needed for a straight line, but a third point is plotted as a check.

sections.heading: Distance–time graphs
sections.body: On a distance–time graph the gradient of each segment is the speed. A steep line is fast, a flat horizontal line means at rest (speed 0), and a downward line means returning.

sections.heading: Solving simultaneous equations
sections.body: A pair of simultaneous equations can be solved three ways. Graphically, the solution is the point where the two lines cross. By elimination, match a variable's coefficient then add or subtract to cancel it. By substitution, make one variable the subject and substitute into the other equation. Parallel lines give no solution; identical lines give infinitely many.

sections.heading: Real-world problems
sections.body: For a word problem, let two letters stand for the two unknowns, form two equations from the given facts, solve them, and state the answer in words.

definitions.definition: Where the line cuts the y-axis (the value of \(y\) when \(x = 0\)).
Two equations solved together for one pair \((x, y)\).
Where two lines cross — the graphical solution.
Adding or subtracting equations to remove one variable.
Expressing one variable in terms of the other, then solving.

examTips: In \(y = mx + c\), the gradient is always the number in front of \(x\) and \(c\) is where it cuts the y-axis.
For elimination, if the matched signs are the SAME, subtract; if OPPOSITE, add.
Two lines with the same gradient but different y-intercepts are parallel → no solution.
